newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, March 7 - CPO production staged a robust recovery in last-half February after dropping some 40 percent in first-half February because of fewer working days arising from the double festive holidays. The speedy recovery was greatly assisted by good to excellent weather conditions in Peninsular Malaysia during the month. On the basis of partial data available, we estimate production declined seasonally by 75,000 tonnes or 13 percent to 502,000 tonnes in February.

Our previous estimate of a 21 percent decline assumed less favourable weather as well as a slow pace in clearing the harvesting backlog caused by work stoppages of up to one week during February 7-14. Plantations in East Malaysia were however less fortunate as widespread excessive rains during the 2nd-half of February further delayed harvesting operations. Not only did production in East Malaysia suffered big double-digit declines, many mills also faced high FFA problems in having to process over-ripe fruits.

Exports, in contrast, turned out to be less than expectations, this shortfall was caused chiefly by vessels delays. We estimate exports of palm oil fell to 440,000 tonnes in February from 552,000 tonnes in January and 468,000 tonnes estimated previously. Poor processing margins faced by refiners also contributed to the lacklustre export performance in February. With offtake exceeding CPO output, stocks of palm oil at end February were further drawn down to an estimated 670,000 tonnes from 696,300 tonnes at end-January and 590-600,000 tonnes estimated previously.

Stocks of CPO are estimated to have dropped some 30,000 tonnes to 325,000 tonnes while PPO stocks rose slightly to an estimated 345,000 tonnes from 340,200 tonnes in January. CPO futures fell 37-42 ringgit in the last one week. Poorer than expected exports coupled with better than estimated production prompted players to liquidate their long positions. Producers/ millers who were undersold were also anxious to sell before price become less attractive. Chart-biased speculative selling was also evident in the last two days which saw CPO futures fell 29-34 ringgit.

May futures settled at 1,234 ringgit yesterday. Cash price averaged 1,346.50 ringgit in February, up from 1,315.50 ringgit in January. Price in January-February averaged 1,331 ringgit, up 98 ringgit or nearly 8 percent over the same period last year. We view the latest decline in price as timely as it would provide the basis for a strong pickup in demand from May onward. Late last night May/June RBD PO/Olein were quoted at $540/$565 respectively.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
